text:
[NTST.3.3] A mock-clock mutation sets the mock clock and is not itself a
sample ([LTIM.2.8.4]): it emits no event and records nothing. The next input
or pump samples the clock source, reads the value the mutation left, and
records it as a `ClockAdvance` carrying both clocks when it differs from the
previous sample ([LTIM.2.8.5], [RFCS.10.1]), with the `DS_EV_TICK` stream
event that sample drives. So a test writes the trace a live run through the
same clock values writes, and two mutations between samples leave one record.

idris.name: Ntst_3_3__event
idris.note: A step of a mock run: a clock move, or an input.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__record_at_samples
idris.note: RECORDED AT SAMPLES, the clauses' reading: a move writes nothing; at an input the sample is recorded if it differs from the one recorded before, by TwoClocks.idr's step. The tick's `DS_EV_TICK` event and `seq` are not modelled.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__consume
idris.note: Consuming an input: the clocks stand, and the engine has consumed one.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__cur
idris.note: The sample the mock holds: its own clocks. In mock mode the engine's clocks are the mock's.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__held
idris.note: THE SAMPLES HELD AT THE INPUTS of a run: one per input, the mock's clocks as they then stand.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__live_at_two
idris.note: A live clock source whose sample at the one input is (2, 2): the values the mock run reaches. A fixture.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__live_trace_is_at_samples
idris.note: THE TRACE RECORDED AT SAMPLES IS THE LIVE ENGINE'S through the same values: TwoClocks.idr's recorder on that source, one input, writes the same two atoms. 'A test writes the trace a live run through the same clock values writes', computed.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__mock_replay_at_mutations
idris.note: RECORDED AT MUTATIONS, A REPLAY FROM ANY STARTING CLOCKS HOLDS AT EVERY INPUT WHAT THE RECORDING HELD, for every mock run. Both readings replay exactly; which trace a mock run leaves is not a question of soundness.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__mock_replay_from
idris.note: Recorded at mutations, a replay whose clocks are the mock's holds what the run held: every move is written as it is made, so the replay's clocks are the mock's at every input.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__mock_traces_differ
idris.note: THE TRACES DIFFER: three atoms recorded at mutations, two at samples -- 'two mutations between samples leave one record' under the clause's recorder, and two under the refused one. Computed.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__record_at_mutations
idris.note: RECORDED AT MUTATIONS, the reading the clause refuses ('emits no event and records nothing'): a move writes a `ClockAdvance` carrying both clocks as it is made; an input writes its record, and before it the first sample if nothing has been recorded yet. Partial because it models a reading the clause rules out; kept so that what is ruled out is computed beside what is required.

idris.name: ntst_3_3__two_moves_then_input
idris.note: Two advances by 1 and then an input, from clocks at (0, 0) before any input: two mutations between samples. A fixture.
